implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: every function gains a final continuation parameter and returns nothing - it computes a value and applies the continuation to it. The entry point supplies the identity continuation, so the transformed program still produces a value for its original caller. Read the result by mentally deleting every trailing lambda. Two variants matter: one-shot continuations (a plain function, used once) and multi-shot continuations (a captured stack, which permits re-entry and is what a generator needs). Optionally defunctionalise - enumerate the continuations of the program as a sum type and replace application with one dispatch function - to get a first-order program.
idiom_name: every function takes a final continuation; returns become applications
pitfalls: A continuation that closes over an accumulator makes the recursion a tail call, which is the point; a continuation that does not re-nests and grows the heap instead.
Partial application of a CPS function defers work to the moment the continuation is supplied, so the evaluation order silently changes.
Escaping a continuation out of its intended lifetime and calling it later is only sound if the captured environment still holds what it needs.
